target_customer: Brands, creative agencies and influencers publishing stories on Snapchat and later Instagram
problem: Teams could not schedule, cross-post or measure Snapchat stories with the tools they used for other social networks.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for social media management
product_category: Social media management for ephemeral stories

founders.name: Sébastien Sikorski
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he built several large consumer apps and teaches at Sciences Po Paris. Education is not stated there.

competitors.name: Snaplytics
competitors.what: Snapchat analytics and influencer tracking platform for brands and agencies
competitors.traction_then: Out of beta in October 2016; one report says over 150 brand clients, undated
competitors.funding_then: Plug and Play accelerator listing dated 2017-03, no amount found

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling and analytics tools on top of Snapchat data. Snapchat offered no open publishing API, so the hard part was working around the platform.

defensibility.rationale: Features were easy to copy and the product depended on a platform that did not support third-party publishing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source states what happened. Instagram launched Stories in 2016, and the company's own page says it shifted to Instagram, but the outcome for the company is not documented.

market_need_then: Brands were moving budget to Snapchat in 2016 and 2017, and analytics vendors such as Snaplytics were launching, which shows demand. The YC pitch described it as Buffer for Snapchat.

branding.domain_note: The snapsuite.com domain, used for the earlier product Snapsuite, now redirects to an unrelated site. No storyboard-branded domain was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: The YC page uses a leading platform marketing voice

rebrands.why: Not stated. The YC page mentions Snapsuite as the earlier product and adds Instagram support, but gives no reason or date.

brand_strength.rationale: Storyboard is a generic word shared with several other companies, and branding searches returned only unrelated Storyboard products.

pivots.to: Storyboard, tools for Instagram and Snapchat stories
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page says Instagram Stories support was planned as an extension.

outcome_analysis: Storyboard started as Snapsuite, a Buffer for Snapchat, and had a single founder in a crowded niche with at least one established analytics rival. No source documents why it went inactive. Platform dependency is the likeliest factor because Snapchat did not offer a publishing API and Instagram Stories copied the format, but this is an inference from the product description, so it is stated cautiously. Funding appears limited to the YC investment.
notes: No company website is listed and snapsuite.com redirects to an unrelated site, so the site is dead. The 120000 USD round rests on one aggregator (village.ai) and is YC's standard deal. CB Insights and Startup Intros list 4.5M to 5M in December 2020 for a company called Storyboard, but nothing ties it to this company, so it is not recorded. Altss labels the YC batch S17 while one aggregator says W17; the YC page says Summer 2017. Cause of failure is not public and the failure factor is an inference. Competitor Snaplytics source is dated 2016-10 and is before the batch.
